thread:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert - HIGH severity - Opal reserved cluster 'opal-reserved-1' p99 latency breach (3.2s) - triggered by latency-monitor

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-5300000123 - opal-reserved-1 p99 latency. PagerDuty escalation started.

Maya (oncall): ack - I'm on it. Looking at graphs now.

Maya (oncall): quick note: customer requests are queuing, 503s are low but clients hitting timeouts. Opal reported slow web responses.

Luca (infra): jumping in — checking reserved pool utilization and KV cache evictions.

Maya (oncall): metrics snapshot: cpu/gpu utilization at 82%, queue length spiked x3 in last 6m, kv_cache_evictions at 14/min (baseline ~1/min).

Maya (oncall): relevant links: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/opal-reserved-1/latency?from=now-30m&to=now (paste), and logs: http://logs.redwood.internal/search?q=opal-reserved-1+evict

Ravi (senior-oncall): I'm up. If kv evictions high, likely memory pressure from a bad batching pattern or long-running requests. Can we check long-lived sequences?

Maya (oncall): grepping tail of router logs now. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:20:11Z router[ingress]: tenant=opal req_id=abcd123 path=/v1/generate latency=3204ms kv_hit=false
2026-03-15T10:21:03Z worker[0]: eviction: key=kv-user-892 freed=24MB reason=cache_pressure
```
Maya (oncall): there's a cluster of requests with seq_len ~4096 hitting unfriendly kernel path. Suspect a model variant with long prefix sequences.

Ravi (senior-oncall): Action plan: 1) enable tenant fallback routing to autopromoted variant (lower memory footprint), 2) temporarily increase reserved-pool headroom for opal-reserved-1 to reduce eviction, 3) throttle/soft-fail long requests. I'll run the fallback step.

Ravi (senior-oncall): running command:
```
redwoodctl routing set --tenant opal --pool opal-reserved-1 --fallback-variant=opti-small --enable
```
incident-bot: Routing policy changed for tenant=opal by Ravi. New fallback variant=opti-small.

Maya (oncall): enabling temporary extra headroom (+2 nodes) via autoscale override:
```
redwoodctl capacity adjust --pool opal-reserved-1 --delta+2 --reason "mitigate p99 latency"
```
Luca (infra): autoscale accepted, provisioning 2 instances (expected ready ~120s).

Opal SRE (customer): Thanks for the quick response. We're seeing client timeouts drop on our end (from 5% down to 1.2%). Will keep monitoring.

Maya (oncall): After fallback + headroom: p99 dropped to 1.1s within ~3m. queue length normalizing. Logging shows reduced kv evictions. :thumbsup:

Maya (oncall): still seeing a smaller tail around specific user flows; I've applied a traffic-class throttle for seq_len > 2048 for Opal to avoid recurrence:
```
redwoodctl policy set --tenant opal --condition "seq_len>2048" --action "retryable_throttle" --rate 0.2
```
Ravi (senior-oncall): good. I'll keep watch for 30m then handoff to Sofia for follow-up and postmortem. Please collect sampling prompts for evals to see if fallback variant changed semantics.

Sofia (next-oncall): ack handoff at 5300000350. I'll take post-incident lead and coordinate with product/rl on customer impact report.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert acknowledged by Maya. Escalation to Ravi acknowledged. Handoff to Sofia scheduled.

Opal SRE (customer): We ran a quick test suite, no observable change in response quality for us after fallback. Appreciate the transparency.

Maya (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Will keep autopromote disabled for now until we run regression eval and labeling.

Ravi (senior-oncall): Note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = recent model variant rollout that increases KV footprint under long prefixes combined with bursty client patterns. Follow-ups: - revert/adjust model variant rollout rules, - add mem-pressure alarm, - add throttling rule for seq_len heavy flows at router.

Sofia (next-oncall): I'll open INC-2026-5300000123-PM doc and link metrics + command run history + sampled prompts. Next steps: schedule sync with Opal SRE tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-5300000123 status: mitigated -> monitoring. PagerDuty: Resolved by Maya.

Maya (oncall): closing thread, will update PM doc with exact timestamps and config diffs. Thanks team. :heart:
